[[Discover Card]] (2017–current) | all_stadiums = | all_locations = }} The '''Big Ten Football Championship Game''' is a [[college football]] game held by the [[Big Ten Conference]] each year to determine the conference's season champion. The game, held after the regular season has been completed, currently matches the top two teams in the conference standings. It is typically held the first Saturday of December, although in 2020 it was played on the third Saturday of December due to the [[COVID-19 pandemic]]. [[Lucas Oil Stadium]] in [[Indianapolis, Indiana]] has been the site of the championship game since its inception in 2011 and is scheduled to host through 2028.{{cite web |first=Will |last=Backas |date=July 23, 2024 |url=https://www.cbssports.com/college-football/news/big-ten-championship-game-will-remain-at-lucas-oil-stadium-in-indianapolis-through-2028/ |title=Big Ten Championship Game will Remain at Lucas Oil Stadium in Indianapolis Through 2028 Season |work=CBS Sports |access-date=Oct 1, 2025}} Since 2017, the game's official title has been the '''Big Ten College Football Championship Game Presented by Discover Card''' following a sponsorship deal with [[Discover Financial]].{{cite news |title=Discover Named Official Credit Card of the Big Ten Conference |url=https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20171107005398/en/ |date=November 7, 2017 |work=BusinessWire.com |access-date=January 26, 2021}} The winner of this game is the Big Ten Champion. The winning team also receives the [[Amos Alonzo Stagg|Stagg]] Championship Trophy, while the most valuable player of the game receives the [[Red Grange|Grange]]–[[Archie Griffin|Griffin]] Championship Game Most Valuable Player Trophy. Through the 2024 game, Wisconsin and Ohio State have the most appearances in the game with six, while Ohio State has the most wins with five. ==History== {{see also|2010–2014 Big Ten Conference realignment}} Prior to the 2011 college football season, the Big Ten Conference determined its conference representative through regular season play, and, as there were only 11 member schools, there was no possibility for a conference championship game because, at the time, the NCAA required that a conference have 12 teams with two divisions in order to hold a conference championship game. [[File:Aerial view of Indianapolis, Indiana, with a focus on Lucas Oil Stadium, highsm.40934.jpg|thumb|right|[[Lucas Oil Stadium]]]] In 2010, the Big Ten Conference added the [[University of Nebraska–Lincoln|University of Nebraska]], bringing the membership total to 12 teams. Thus, the conference was able to meet NCAA requirements. On August 5, 2010, Big Ten Conference Commissioner [[James Delany]] announced that [[Lucas Oil Stadium]] in [[Indianapolis, Indiana]] had been chosen as the possible site for the inaugural championship game. The league office began a 30-day period to negotiate a one-year agreement with Indiana Sports Corp and Lucas Oil Stadium to host the game. Delany also announced that once the 2011 agreement was in place, the conference office would conduct a thorough process over the next year to determine the location of the Big Ten Football Championship Game in 2012 and beyond.{{cite web |url=http://www.bigten.org/sports/m-footbl/spec-rel/080510aab.html |title=Indianapolis' Lucas Oil Stadium Selected as Proposed Site for 2011 Big Ten Football Championship Game |publisher=BigTen.org: The Big Ten Conference Official Site |date=August 5, 2010 |access-date=August 5, 2010 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100823182140/http://www.bigten.org/sports/m-footbl/spec-rel/080510aab.html |archive-date=23 August 2010 |url-status=dead }} On November 17, 2010, the Big Ten Conference announced a media agreement with [[Fox Sports (USA)|Fox Sports]] to serve as the official broadcast partner for the 2011–2016 Big Ten Football Championship Games. A source at the time stated that the six-year agreement with Fox Sports would be worth between $20–$25 million per season, making it one of the most valuable conference championship games in college football.{{cite web|url=http://www.chicagobreakingsports.com/2010/11/soldier-field-good-bet-to-host-big-ten-title-game.html |title=Soldier Field good bet to host Big Ten title game |publisher=ChicagoBreakingSports.com |date=November 18, 2010 |access-date=November 18, 2010}} In the league's press release, it was confirmed that the 2011 event would take place at Lucas Oil Stadium in [[prime time]]. Because Fox is a majority partner in the [[Big Ten Network]],{{cite web|url=http://www.mediapost.com/publications/article/157692/fox-moves-to-majority-position-in-big-ten-network.html#axzz2DBJFtjus |title=MediaPost Publications Fox Moves to Majority Position in Big Ten Network 08/30/2011 |publisher=Mediapost.com |access-date=2014-06-06}} this may allow for the possibility of more involvement by the Big Ten Network in the event, including the use of Big Ten Network staff in the game coverage.{{cite web |url=http://www.bigten.org/sports/m-footbl/spec-rel/111710aaa.html |title=Big Ten Announces Media Agreement with Fox Sports to Televise 2011-16 Big Ten Football Championship Games |publisher=BigTen.org: The Big Ten Conference Official Site |date=November 17, 2010 |access-date=November 17, 2010 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20101223112326/http://www.bigten.org/sports/m-footbl/spec-rel/111710aaa.html |archive-date=23 December 2010 |url-status=dead }} Commissioner Delany also stated at that time that the Big Ten would strongly consider rotating the site of the game, mentioning other possible host cities such as Chicago, Detroit, Minneapolis, Green Bay, and Cleveland. On June 5, 2014, the Big Ten Conference announced via press release that the Big Ten Football Championship game would continue to be held at Lucas Oil Stadium through the 2024 season.{{cite web |last=Axson |first=Scooby |url=http://tracking.si.com/2014/06/05/big-ten-football-championship-indianapolis-basketball-tournament-chicago/ |title=Big Ten announces future sites for football championship game, basketball tournaments | SI Wire |publisher=Tracking.si.com |date=2014-05-13 |access-date=2014-06-06 |archive-date=2014-06-08 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140608010443/http://tracking.si.com/2014/06/05/big-ten-football-championship-indianapolis-basketball-tournament-chicago/ |url-status=dead }}{{cite web |url=http://www.bigten.org/sports/m-footbl/spec-rel/060514aaa.html |title=Big Ten Announces Extension of Football Championship Games in Indianapolis and Basketball Tournaments in Chicago and Indianapolis - BIG TEN CONFERENCE Official Athletic Site |publisher=Bigten.org |access-date=2014-06-06 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140820135156/http://www.bigten.org/sports/m-footbl/spec-rel/060514aaa.html |archive-date=2014-08-20 |url-status=dead }} ==Conference expansion== The Big Ten expanded to 11 schools by adding [[Pennsylvania State University|Penn State]] in 1990,{{cite web |url=http://www.bigten.org/sports/wchamp25/spec-rel/091106aaa.html |title=An Ingenious Inception: Penn State Joins the Big Ten Conference |publisher=BigTen.org: The Big Ten Conference Official Site |date=September 11, 2006 |access-date=November 24, 2010 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110311004727/http://www.bigten.org/sports/wchamp25/spec-rel/091106aaa.html |archive-date=March 11, 2011 |url-status=dead }} but this did not yet meet the [[National Collegiate Athletic Association|NCAA]]'s requirements for holding a conference championship game (that the conference have 12 teams with two divisions). A few other times during that period, there were talks between the Big Ten and other schools (namely, [[University of Kansas|Kansas]], [[University of Missouri|Missouri]], and [[Rutgers University|Rutgers]],{{cite news|url=https://www.chicagotribune.com/1993/12/10/kansas-big-10-a-good-fit/ |title=Kansas, Big 10 a good fit? |publisher=Chicago Tribune |date=December 10, 1993 |access-date=November 24, 2010 |first=Ed |last=Sherman}} and later [[University of Notre Dame|Notre Dame]]{{cite news|url=https://findarticles.com/p/articles/mi_m1141/is_16_35/ai_80680415/print |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20050528030211/http://findarticles.com/p/articles/mi_m1141/is_16_35/ai_80680415/print |url-status=usurped |archive-date=May 28, 2005 |title=Notre Dame shuns Big Ten, fears losing 'distinctiveness' |publisher=National Catholic Reporter |issue=16 |volume=35 |date=February 19, 1999 |access-date=November 24, 2010}}) which might have led to the possibility of a conference with two divisions of at least six teams and a conference championship, but for various reasons, nothing came to fruition. It was not until December 2009, when Commissioner Delany announced that the league would explore the possibility of adding one or more institutions, that the wheels were set in motion that would lead to the Big Ten adding a school for the first time in 20 years. Less than a year later, on June 11, 2010, [[University of Nebraska–Lincoln|Nebraska]] applied for membership and was unanimously accepted by the conference's 11 member schools. Its membership became effective on July 1, 2011.{{cite web |url=http://www.bigten.org/genrel/061110aab.html |title=University of Nebraska Approved to Join Big Ten Conference by Council of Presidents/Chancellors' |publisher=BigTen.org: The Big Ten Conference Official Site |date=June 11, 2010 |access-date=November 24, 2010 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20101222184204/http://www.bigten.org/genrel/061110aab.html |archive-date=22 December 2010 |url-status=dead }} In [[2010–2014 Big Ten Conference realignment#Maryland|November 2012]], the Big Ten announced that [[University of Maryland, College Park|Maryland]]{{cite press release |url=http://www.bigten.org/genrel/111912aac.html |title=University Of Maryland To Join The Big Ten Conference |publisher=Big Ten Conference |date=November 19, 2012 |access-date=November 19, 2013 |archive-date=May 18, 2013 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130518074806/http://www.bigten.org/genrel/111912aac.html |url-status=dead }} and [[Rutgers University|Rutgers]]{{cite press release |url=http://www.bigten.org/genrel/112012aaf.html |title=Rutgers University To Join The Big Ten Conference |publisher=Big Ten Conference |date=November 20, 2012 |access-date=November 19, 2013 |archive-date=November 27, 2012 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121127180040/http://www.bigten.org/genrel/112012aaf.html |url-status=dead }} would join the conference in 2014, which brought conference membership up to 14 schools. The Big Ten [[2021–2024 NCAA conference realignment|expanded further in 2024]], first announcing in 2022 that [[UCLA Bruins football|UCLA]] and [[USC Trojans football|USC]] would join in 2024{{cite press release|url=https://bigten.org/news/2022/6/30/general-big-ten-conference-statement.aspx |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220701003507/https://bigten.org/news/2022/6/30/general-big-ten-conference-statement.aspx |url-status=dead |archive-date=July 1, 2022 |title=Big Ten Conference Statement |publisher=Big Ten Conference |date=June 30, 2022 |access-date=June 30, 2022}} and then announcing the next year that [[Oregon Ducks football|Oregon]] and [[Washington Huskies football|Washington]] would join alongside UCLA and USC.{{cite press release|url=https://bigten.org/news/2023/8/4/general-big-ten.aspx |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230804223113/https://bigten.org/news/2023/8/4/general-big-ten.aspx |url-status=dead |archive-date=August 4, 2023 |title=University of Oregon and University of Washington to Join Big Ten Conference in 2024 |publisher=Big Ten Conference |date=August 4, 2023 |access-date=August 4, 2023}} ==Team selection== {{OSM Location map | nolabels = 1 | coord = {{coord|41.7831235|-85.4343115}} | zoom = 5 | width = 575 | height = 300 | caption = [[File:Blue pog.svg|10px]] – East division

label-color15 = black }} Through the 2023 edition, the participating teams in the game were the first place teams from each of the conference's two divisions. Starting in 2024, the game featured the top two teams in the conference standings. After the addition of Nebraska to the conference, there was much debate over what would be the best division of the 12 schools. Some felt that it would be best to maintain geographical divisions. Others felt that geography should only be a factor insofar as there was competitive balance between the two divisions. Another very important factor for Big Ten schools was the maintenance of long-standing rivalries that the schools held with each other. On September 1, 2010, Commissioner Delany revealed how the teams would be placed into the two divisions.{{cite web|url=http://www.chicagobreakingsports.com/2010/09/big-ten-divisions-to-be-revealed-on-6-pm-tv-show.html |title=Big Ten sets new divisions; splits up Illinois-NU |publisher=ChicagoBreakingSports.com |date=September 1, 2010 |access-date=November 24, 2010 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100904033515/http://www.chicagobreakingsports.com/2010/09/big-ten-divisions-to-be-revealed-on-6-pm-tv-show.html |archive-date=September 4, 2010 }} On December 13, Commissioner Delany announced that the two divisions would be called Legends and Leaders.{{cite web |url=http://www.bigten.org/sports/m-footbl/spec-rel/080411aaa.html |title=Big Ten Conference Reveals New Logo and Honors Football History with Division Names and Trophies |publisher=BigTen.org: The Big Ten Conference Official Site |date=December 13, 2010 |access-date=December 13, 2010 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110822203918/http://www.bigten.org/sports/m-footbl/spec-rel/080411aaa.html |archive-date=August 22, 2011 |url-status=dead }} The scheduling arrangement for the schools was that they would face each of the other schools in their division, plus three crossover opponents, one of which would be permanent. The permanent crossover opponent would be used to ensure that long standing historical rivalries would continue. On August 4, 2011, the Big Ten Conference announced that there would be a nine-game conference schedule beginning in 2017, allowing schools to play four crossover opponents.{{cite web |url=http://www.bigten.org/newlogo |title=Big Ten Schools to Play Nine Conference Games Beginning With 2017 Season |publisher=BigTen.org: The Big Ten Conference Official Site |date=August 4, 2011 |access-date=August 4, 2011 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110725073514/http://www.bigten.org/newlogo/ |archive-date=July 25, 2011 |url-status=dead }} However, the Big Ten and [[Pac-12 Conference|Pac-12]] later announced a multi-sport scheduling agreement that provides for each member school to play one non-conference football game per year against an opponent from the other conference, and with this announcement, the Big Ten backed away from the nine-game conference schedule proposal. Following the 2014 entry of Maryland and Rutgers, the "Leaders" and "Legends" divisions were set aside and replaced by geographic divisions, with the schools in the [[Central Time Zone]] plus Purdue forming the new West Division, and the remaining members forming the East Division. In addition, the conference adopted a nine-game schedule beginning in 2016.{{cite press release |url=http://www.bigten.org/sports/m-footbl/spec-rel/042813aaa.html |title=Big Ten Announces Football Division Alignments and Move to Nine-Game Conference Schedules |publisher=Big Ten Conference |date=April 28, 2013 |access-date=November 19, 2013 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130804022458/http://www.bigten.org/sports/m-footbl/spec-rel/042813aaa.html |archive-date=August 4, 2013 |url-status=dead }} In December 2020, the Big Ten Conference waived the six-game minimum requirement for a team to participate in the championship game; Ohio State, which had a 5–0 record after playing a limited schedule impacted by the [[COVID-19 pandemic in the United States]], would otherwise have been ineligible to participate. The Big Ten stated, "The decision was based on a competitive analysis which determined that Ohio State would have advanced to the Big Ten Football Championship Game based on its undefeated record and head-to-head victory over Indiana regardless of a win or loss against Michigan."{{cite news |url=https://bigten.org/news/2020/12/9/ohio-state-will-advance-to-big-ten-football-championship-game.aspx |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201209211232/https://bigten.org/news/2020/12/9/ohio-state-will-advance-to-big-ten-football-championship-game.aspx |url-status=dead |archive-date=December 9, 2020 |title=Ohio State will Advance to Big Ten Football Championship Game |website=[[Big Ten Conference]] |date=December 9, 2020 |access-date=December 9, 2020}} With the conference [[2021–2024 NCAA conference realignment|expanding to 18 teams]] in 2024 with the arrival of [[Oregon Ducks football|Oregon]], [[UCLA Bruins football|UCLA]], [[USC Trojans football|USC]], and [[Washington Huskies football|Washington]], the divisions were eliminated effective at that time.{{cite press release |url=https://bigten.org/fb/article/blt39fc5a9dd81251cf/ |title=Big Ten Conference Announces Future Football Schedule Formats for 2024-28 |publisher=Big Ten Conference |date=October 4, 2023 |access-date=October 30, 2023}} {{clear}} ==Results== {| class="wikitable sortable" style="text-align:center" |- ! style="background:#0088cd; color:#FFFFFF; border:2px solid #000000;"|Miscellaneous ! style="background:#0088cd; color:#FFFFFF; border:2px solid #000000;"|Record, Team vs. Team ! style="background:#0088cd; color:#FFFFFF; border:2px solid #000000;"|Year |- |Game attendance || 68,214, Ohio State vs. Indiana || 2025 |- |} Source:{{cite web|title=Indianapolis to Continue Hosting Big Ten Football Championship Game…|url=https://www.indianasportscorp.org/news/indianapolis-to-continue-hosting-big-ten-football-championship-game-through-2028#:~:text=This%20announcement%20follows%20a%20record,since%20its%20inception%20in%202011. |pages=1|website=[[Indiana Sport Corp.]] |via= |access-date=December 8, 2025}} ==Selection criteria== On September 1, 2011, the Big Ten Conference announced the divisional tiebreaker procedures that will be used to determine the representatives in the championship game.{{cite web |url=http://www.bigten.org/sports/m-footbl/archive/081011aaa.html# |title=Big Ten Conference Football Divisional Tiebreaker |publisher=BigTen.org: The Big Ten Conference Official Site |date=September 1, 2011 |access-date=September 1, 2011 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110823111226/http://www.bigten.org/sports/m-footbl/archive/081011aaa.html |archive-date=August 23, 2011 |url-status=dead }} Division standings are based on each team's overall conference record, excluding teams ineligible for postseason because of sanctions. In the event that two teams are tied, the head-to-head results between those two teams determines the tiebreaker. Unlike the Southeastern Conference, whose rules were established before NCAA overtime and has provisions in case the two tied teams' game is either canceled or tied because of inclement weather (NCAA rules permit drawn games if, after three periods have been played, a game is tied when the game is called off because of inclement weather, including reaching curfew), the Big Ten does not have a policy in case the head-to-head result is a tie because of inclement weather. ===Three or more-team tiebreaker procedure=== If only two teams remain after any of the following steps, the tiebreaker will revert to the two-team tiebreaker above. # The records of the three or more tied teams will be compared against each other. # The records of the three or more tied teams will be compared within their division. # The records of the three or more tied teams will be compared against the next highest placed teams in their division in order of finish (4, 5, 6, and 7). # The records of the three or more tied teams will be compared against all common conference opponents. # The team with the best overall winning percentage (excluding exempted games) will be the representative. # The representative will be chosen by random draw. ==See also== * [[List of NCAA Division I FBS conference championship games]] ==Notes== {{reflist|group=n}} ==References== {{Reflist|2}} {{Big Ten Football Championship Game navbox}} {{Big Ten Conference football navbox}} {{Big Ten championships navbox}} {{NCAA Division I FBS conference championship game navbox}} [[Category:Big Ten Football Championship Game| ]] [[Category:Recurring sporting events established in 2011]] [[Category:2011 establishments in Indiana]] [[Category:Sports competitions in Indianapolis]]
